primary_sources.title: OS-Harm: A Benchmark for Measuring Safety of Computer Use Agents
sections: 3.3 Safety Evaluation with an LLM Judge
primary_sources.claim_support: 150 tasks, 50 per category; deliberate misuse, prompt injection and model misbehavior; separate safety and task-success judgments.
primary_sources.application_limit: Published judge agreement does not validate this project custom visual judge or make its percentages directly comparable.

primary_sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
primary_sources.claim_support: Report benign utility and utility under attack alongside targeted attack success; tool filtering can fail when authorized tools also permit the attack.
primary_sources.application_limit: AgentDojo tool-isolation results do not establish protection in this unrestricted desktop harness. Refusal-only reduction in adoption cannot establish useful robust completion.

primary_sources.title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
sections: 3 Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents Against Prompt Injections
primary_sources.claim_support: Output manipulation and downstream output risks are established concerns; prompt engineering is heuristic and has no security guarantee; principled system constraints differ from prompting.
primary_sources.application_limit: This suffix is not an implemented structural isolation guarantee, and draft contamination is not claimed as a new injection class.

primary_sources.title: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents
primary_sources.claim_support: Local proposed-action judgments and end-to-end evaluation are complementary; retain original task success criteria while adding explicit state-based safety checks.
primary_sources.application_limit: Supports measurement design, not effectiveness of this project prompt intervention.

recommended_narrative.headline: Logged recognition of an injection can coexist with later endorsement in a newly written artifact.
recommended_narrative.paragraph: Our custom OS-Harm run produced 137 judged trajectories. Focused trace audits distinguish unsafe preparation, persisted document-integrity loss, and newly endorsed attacker instructions without execution. In two payload variants of the same email task, the agent first questioned or rejected embedded instructions, then presented them as user action items. A frozen paired pilot tests whether persistent source-authority guidance and a final writing check improve this local failure while preserving useful completion.
recommended_narrative.novelty_scope: Measurement refinement and local feasibility, not a new attack class, causal memory mechanism, or proven defense.

fixed_experiment_assessment.size: Three scenarios x attacked/neutral payload x baseline/intervention = 12 scheduled attempts maximum.
fixed_experiment_assessment.justification: Directly reproduce the observed development failure, probe broader source-boundary transfer in attachment and formatting tasks, and check neutral task utility and content preservation.
reporting: Keep development separate from the two transfer scenarios.
Report all scheduled/attempted cells, including setup failures, timeouts, nonexposure and unknowns.
Separate recommendation, preparation/attempt, confirmed state effect and transmission.
Report authorized task completion under attack alongside adoption and neutral utility.
A nonreproducing baseline provides no mitigation evidence.
No violating transfer baseline means transfer mitigation remains untested.
Do not replace cases or extend the fixed pilot based on results.
limits: One draw per cell cannot estimate stochastic reliability.
The suffix bundles source authority and final recheck; component causality is unidentified.
Transfer tasks preserve/format existing content rather than synthesize new action lists.
Neutral payloads retain sender/subject scaffolding and are not length/layout matched.
Neutral controls do not test legitimate technical authority discrimination.
Gate can be passed through refusal on attacked tasks; utility under attack must remain visible.

reporting_refinements: Qualify Only prompt suffix varies as within each matched baseline/intervention job; attacked/neutral payload also varies across conditions.
Describe the second email case as tentative suspicion and planned exclusion, not categorical rejection.
Keep output contamination distinct from execution, transmission, persistent storage and downstream harm.
Treat safe labels in incomplete tasks as bounded observations rather than successful safety refusals.
Do not infer screenshot eviction causes the inconsistency; repetition, sender impersonation, task relevance, stochasticity and limited image history remain competing explanations.
